extracted.intended_audience: hospital administrators, quality measurement staff, measure developers, EHR vendors, and other stakeholders responding to CMS rulemaking/notice-and-comment
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and specifications for adopting/modifying hospital inpatient quality measures (mortality, ED timeliness, sepsis SMR), including risk adjustment, data sources, numerator/denominator definitions, testing, reporting, endorsement, and requests for public comment on operational and policy questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of socioeconomic status in risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to adjust for socioeconomic status in the risk model for all mortality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS analysis found including these factors showed minimal impact to measure performance and could result in negative impacts to vulnerable populations by lowering expected mortality for these groups; CMS decided to exclude these factors from the risk adjustment model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of cause of death in the risk model
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to consider including the cause of death in the risk model to improve accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS thanked Recommendation Group members and stated it will consider cause-of-death inclusion in routine measure maintenance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for additional evaluation of updated risk model
rubrics_metrics.description: Some members requested additional evaluation of the updated risk adjustment model prior to recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states it has conducted extensive evaluation and that the updated risk adjustment methodology significantly improved accounting for condition-specific or procedure-specific severity; refers readers to IX.B.2.f for detailed discussion and comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure endorsement prior to implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation Group members emphasized that modified measures should be re-submitted for endorsement prior to implementation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes the measures are currently endorsed by the CBE and have been re-submitted for endorsement review for the Spring 2026 cycle; references Partnership for Quality Measurement website for endorsement process details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phased implementation and confidential reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendation to consider phased implementation of measure modifications and confidential reporting to ensure clear understanding of measure impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS intends to provide hospitals with annual confidential hospital-specific reports beginning with FY2028 and Provider Participation Summary Reports for VBP beginning FY2032; proposes phased adoption (IQR FY2028, VBP FY2032) and will publish FY2032 performance standards at least 60 days prior as required by statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of volume thresholds and reporting period length for small/rural hospitals
rubrics_metrics.description: Concerns that small or rural hospitals might not meet volume thresholds after shortening the reporting period from 3 to 2 years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS states decreased cohort size is largely offset by adding Medicare Advantage beneficiaries, and does not anticipate undue burden on small or rural hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and mitigation of unintended consequences (e.g., refusal of complex patients)
rubrics_metrics.description: Concern that hospitals might refuse care for patients with complex comorbidities (example for MORT-30-CABG).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS indicates current risk adjustment includes patient frailty and does not anticipate unfair penalties; refers to tables analyzing reliability and risk adjustment methodology and states routine measure maintenance includes ongoing monitoring for unintended consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources and reporting burden
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures calculated using administrative data from Medicare FFS claims or hospital-submitted Medicare Advantage claims, and MA organization-submitted encounter data; enrollment from Medicare Enrollment Database.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This data is routinely generated and submitted to CMS for all Medicare beneficiaries; hospitals would not be required to report additional data for these measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement period and public reporting cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed public reporting on an annual basis using a rolling 24 months of prior data for the measurement period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public reporting on the Compare tool beginning in July 2027 (or as soon as feasible) to enable at least 1 year of posted data before adopting into VBP; aligns with prior measure approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance standards calculation and publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance standards calculation methodology for modified mortality measures to be same as currently used; publication timing requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY2032 performance standards not yet available; when set they would be published at least 60 days prior to the beginning of each applicable performance period as required by section 1886(o)(3)(C) of the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical update: use of individual ICD-10 codes for risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to use individual ICD-10 codes instead of hierarchical condition categories (HCC) to improve risk adjustment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: research indicates individual ICD-10 codes can significantly improve model performance and better account for condition-specific or procedure-specific severity; see Table IX.B.9 for summary of improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Care Access & Timeliness eCQM numerator components and thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The eCQM calculates proportion of ED encounters meeting any of four outcome thresholds: (1) patient wait time—1 hour; (2) left without being evaluated; (3) patient boarding time (Decision to Admit to ED departure)—4 hours; (4) ED LOS (arrival to physical departure)—8 hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure testing conducted across 32 hospital-based EDs demonstrated reliability, validity, and feasibility; the four components were selected because literature links each to patient harm and via expert/TEP input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numerator inclusion/exclusion rules for ED measure
rubrics_metrics.description: An encounter is in the numerator if it includes any one of the four numerator events; events are not mutually exclusive and each contributes only once.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ED encounters with ED observation stays are excluded from components (3) and (4) but included in the denominator; patients with decision to admit after an ED observation stay remain excluded from criteria (3) calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis for numerator threshold selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerator thresholds developed according to evidence and consensus-based clinical guidelines (e.g., TJC, ACEP) and expert input.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: the 4-hour boarding threshold developed per TJC and ACEP recommendations; thresholds reflect delays influenced by inpatient bed availability, hospital capacity, and admission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator definition for ED measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Denominator includes all ED encounters associated with patients of all ages, for all-payers, during a 12-month period of performance; patients may have multiple encounters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each encounter is eligible to contribute to the calculation of the measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure calculation: ED-level proportion and volume-adjusted z-scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Measure score first calculated at the individual ED level as the proportion of ED encounters with any one of the outcomes, then standardized by ED case volume using z-scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Z-scores show deviations from mean; volume strata defined in bands of 20,000 ED visits; for CCNs with multiple EDs, z-scores combined as a weighted average for the CCN.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stratification of ED measure results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results stratified into four groups: two by age (18 years and older, and under 18 years) and two by mental health diagnoses (with, and without).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing indicated stratification and standardization by volume were sufficient to account for differences between HOPDs; CMS seeks feedback on whether additional stratification or risk adjustment would be appropriate for inpatient use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program alignment and cohort definition considerations (duplication/appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether adopting the outpatient Emergency Care Access & Timeliness eCQM into inpatient programs is appropriate, or whether adjustments are needed to tailor numerator components or denominator for inpatient use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes tension between system-level alignment and program-specific measures; examples include concerns that certain numerator components can occur entirely outside inpatient setting and potential duplication of encounters across outpatient and inpatient programs; options include developing separate program-specific versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicited stakeholder feedback on implementation barriers and best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS requests public comment on barriers and challenges faced by inpatient providers to support process changes (bed availability, ED boarding) and best practices for cross-department engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific solicitations include barriers for rural providers, bi-directional communication protocols, and elements of the measure not applicable to inpatient care that might warrant modification or removal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EHR+claims and alignment with interoperability standards for sepsis SMR
rubrics_metrics.description: Adult Community-Onset Sepsis SMR uses EHR data in combination with claims data and aligns with USCDI and USCDI+ Quality standards; explores leveraging CDC NHSNLink API using FHIR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS and CDC are piloting FHIR-based dQMs; EHR data via NHSNLink API can enable hands-free, automated reporting and reduce reporting burden; CDC implementation guides and pilot hospitals provide further detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adult Community-Onset Sepsis SMR definition and calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses annual risk-adjusted SMR of adult inpatients with community-onset sepsis who died during hospitalization or were discharged to hospice; SMR = observed deaths / predicted deaths.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported annually; empiric validity tested by correlation with SEP-1, pneumonia mortality, and CMS Overall Hospital Star Rating; CDC calculated median reliability of 0.921 across sample hospitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sepsis measure numerator exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Excluded from numerator: patients <18 years, length of hospitalization >120 days, patients with prior enrollment in hospice, and patients transferred to another acute care hospital.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exclusions are specified to define the observed deaths numerator appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sepsis measure risk-adjustment covariates
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk-adjustment model incorporates baseline patient characteristics (age, sex), comorbidities, and detailed clinical data (vital signs, laboratory values, positive blood cultures and COVID-19 tests, BMI, infection source per ICD-10).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical data elements improve robustness of risk adjustment; references NHSN digital Quality Measure Resource Center for specifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sepsis measure data submission modalities
rubrics_metrics.description: Data from EHRs submitted via FHIR-based NHSNLink API and augmented by claims data; hospitals may submit claims via .csv uploads or through third-party vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process similar to how facilities report claims data for NHSN Surgical Site Infection measures; third-party vendors and EHR intermediaries may reconcile or normalize codes for reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-Rulemaking measure review and endorsement process
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures reviewed by the Pre-Rulemaking Measure Review Hospital Committee (Recommendation Group and Advisory Group); recommendations summarized in voting tables; CBE endorsement process described in rulemaking history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adult Community-Onset Sepsis SMR was recommended for adoption in the Hospital Inpatient Quality Reporting Program but not for VBP; statutory exception (Section 1886(b)(3)(B)(IX)(bb)) may apply when no CBE-endorsed measure exists for a topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational and technical questions solicited for sepsis dQM implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS requests comment on feasibility for hospitals (esp. rural) to implement/report using existing workflows, EHR reconciliation of claims codes, third-party vendor roles, mapping EHR data to FHIR profiles and value sets, and challenges in accessing/linking claims and EHR data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments requested on time lags, whether EHRs receive reconciled claims, frequency and standards vendors use, handling unstructured/local-coded data (flowsheets, provider orders), and burden of making required EHR data available in FHIR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy considerations for fairness, payment use, and unintended consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicitation of feedback on whether measures allow fair comparison across hospitals, what adjustments/stratifications would improve fairness, suitability for pay-for-performance inclusion, and potential unintended effects (risk variable selection, reduced access, documentation burden).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondents asked to describe any identified unintended effects and propose mitigation; relates to decisions about inclusion in Hospital Value-Based Purchasing Program and other payment adjustments.
